source.quote: Speaking for the United States and Japan after the vote, Mr. Wood explained that extending the Secretary-General’s reporting would provide the Council with accurate and timely information for future deliberations on the Houthi attacks. He said attacks threatened commerce and the flow of humanitarian assistance. Both co-sponsors voted in favour.

Mr. Bendjama said Algeria abstained, consistent with its January vote. It continued to value the Secretary-General’s monthly reports on attacks on merchant and commercial vessels for keeping the Council informed. Algeria attributed its abstention to concerns over implementation of resolution 2722 (2024) and what it regarded as misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign countries’ territory.

overlap.response: The United States and Japan supported extending reporting for accurate information on Houthi attacks, while Algeria abstained citing concerns over resolution implementation and misuse of self-defence.

source.quote: Operative paragraph 1 of resolution 2739 extends the Secretary-General’s reporting request under paragraph 10 of resolution 2722 (2024) until 15 January 2025. The resolution also reiterates its demand that the Houthis cease attacks on merchant and commercial vessels and release the Galaxy Leader and its crew. It urges caution, restraint and diplomatic efforts. The adopted text contains no new authorization of military action or expansion of the reporting authority.

Mr. Bendjama said Algeria abstained, consistent with its January vote. It continued to value the Secretary-General’s monthly reports on attacks on merchant and commercial vessels for keeping the Council informed. Algeria attributed its abstention to concerns over implementation of resolution 2722 (2024) and what it regarded as misuse or misinterpretation of self-defence through attacks on sovereign countries’ territory.

overlap.response: Algeria's assessment of misuse in self-defence justified its abstention, while the adopted action extended reporting and reiterated demands without new military authorization.
overlap.reason: The action text and Algeria's statement support a contrast between the adopted action and the abstention, but supply no sponsor reporting rationale to connect.
